evidence.requirements: Nearly every brief item is implemented. The start page has the heading, Search (input event), Family select, '<n> cartridges' count and name links (app.js:52-104, list.jpg). The detail page has the facts, capacity with source link, grouped Symbol/Value/Unit tables, the Print button and 'All cartridges' (app.js:133-173). Hash routes survive a reload (app.js:20-42). The SVG has role=img with the label '<name> drawing' (drawing.js:295). Every dimension the brief lists is drawn, including α (drawing.js:156-234). The title block has the name, table and revision, 'Dimensions in mm' and a scale bar. Print is one A4 page with a footer (print-308_win.jpg). Partly met: (1) the title block's scale says 'Scale 1:1' (drawing.js:246), which is false on screen and in print, where the drawing is scaled to the page width. (2) Drawing labels deliberately leave out tolerances, e.g. 'L1 39.62' with no -0.2 (drawing.js:128-131), against the brief's 'show it next to the value' rule. (3) Phone legibility is unproven. Labels are a fixed 3 mm in a viewBox of about 115 mm, so they are about 10 px wide on a 375 px screen, and there is no phone screenshot or test. (4) Missing values are noted ('Not drawn: …'), but fillet radii that don't fit are silently reduced (geometry.js:74-78) instead of being reported.
evidence.correctness: The geometry follows the rules closely. Rim type (geometry.js:24-33), chamfer (173-176), the rimfire half-round with its apex at R1/2 (163-171), groove floor and ramp (189-210), the belt ramp at δ (200-206), body and shoulder with r1 min / r2 fillets (227-237), and the straight case to (H2/2, L3) all match. So do the seating and cylinder factors (37-51), the tangent ogive ρ and centre (283-290), the quarter-ellipse and cone noses, and the heeled bullet using H2 and H2-2tb (272-274). Walls tn/tb, the w maximum, and pocket diameters and depths match too (349-373). Compared with the references, the screenshot outlines and proportions are right: 308 shoulder and neck, 300 WM belt and groove, 9 mm taper and round nose, 22 LR rim and heeled bullet, 44 Mag SWC cone. Values and DMS angles match the data ('10°58'00"', '71°25'59"'). Defects: (1) 'Scale 1:1' is wrong. (2) The diameter extension lines start at the feature and run horizontally to the right-hand columns (drawing.js:214-215). For 308 that puts the E1 line (r=5.195, starting at z=2.77) inside the body outline for its whole length and across the shoulder and section walls. It shows as doubled lines along the body in detail-308_win.jpg and detail-300_win_mag.jpg. (3) The R dimension arrowheads (1.8 mm) overlap on a 1.27–1.52 mm span (the 'R 1.37' blob). Print fits one A4 page (print-308_win.jpg; e2e test runs all 25).
evidence.security: The SVG is built as a string and assigned with innerHTML (app.js:149). Names and labels pass through escapeXml (drawing.js:285-287, 295, 320) and numbers through String(). The pattern id `hatch-${d.key}` (drawing.js:292) puts a data field into markup unescaped; it is harmless for this data but inconsistent. All other DOM is built with textContent/setAttribute (app.js:6-18). There is no eval, no fetch, no CDN and no fonts.
evidence.code_quality: Files are split by responsibility: format.js, catalogue.js, geometry.js (model), drawing.js (layout and SVG), app.js (routing and views). Function names are clear and the small el() helper is used consistently. Missing values produce explicit notes and an unknown key shows a not-found view. Weak points: every function is a global through classic scripts (justified by file://), buildDrawing is a 140-line function with layout constants, and labelConflicts is test-only logic shipped in app code.
evidence.tests: The unit tests cover rim type, primer pockets, tn/tb, w, chamfer, groove, belt, rimfire half-round, fillet existence, straight case, heeled bullet, pointy/rounded/SWC bullet parameters, tangent-ogive geometry, missing-value notes, section pocket and inner mouth, and NaN-free models for all 25 records (geometry.test.js). They also check label overlaps for all 25 drawings and the required 308 labels (drawing.test.js), plus formatting, tolerances, symbols, units and sections (format.test.js), filtering (catalogue.test.js) and data identity (data.test.js). The Playwright e2e tests cover the list, search, filter, routing and reload, detail, not-found, dark/print colours, and one A4 page for every record. Gaps: no flat-nose (40 S&W) test, the 'α/2' test checks the data rather than the drawing (geometry.test.js:114-119), extension lines crossing the outline go unchecked, and nothing tests phone width.
evidence.ux_design: The facts and tables are dense, calm and tabular (detail-308_win.jpg). Printing works well: a four-column facts grid, the drawing at full width and three-column tables (print-308_win.jpg). The drawing is the weak part. Text sizes are fixed in mm, so they swing with cartridge length: on 22 LR and 9 mm the labels are ~35 px and the title block is bigger than the page H1 and the drawing itself (detail-22_long_rifle.jpg, detail-9_mm_luger.jpg). On long rifle cases the cartridge is a thin strip under a tall stack of dimensions (detail-9_3_x_74_r.jpg). Extension lines double the body outline, and section hatching on the thin walls is barely visible. Dark mode is in the CSS but there is no screenshot of it.
evidence.accessibility: The SVG has role=img with the label '<name> drawing'. Tables use th scope=col and scope=row. Inputs are wrapped in visible labels, the filter group has role=search and the count is aria-live (app.js:74-78). There are :focus-visible outlines (style.css:47-50) and lang=en. Muted text #5f6670 on #fbfbf9 is about 5.9:1. The drawing's text alternative is only its name, with no summary of the dimensions (the tables partly make up for this), and the tables have no caption or aria-labelledby pointing at their h3.
evidence.simplicity: There are no runtime dependencies and one dev dependency (Playwright, pinned). Six small classic scripts total roughly 1,000 lines. The data build script is 37 lines. The amount of code fits the task.
evidence.maintainability: The README gives open/run, data rebuild and test commands, Playwright is pinned exactly and there is a package-lock. There is no CI configuration, no Node engine pin (.nvmrc or engines), no changelog or release process beyond 'version 1.0.0', and no ADRs or docs. The README points to '.scratch/cartridge-reference/spec.md' for the drawing-rule interpretations (README.md:21), but that file is not in the repository. The e2e tests need a manual 'npx playwright install chromium' step, which the README does mention.
evidence.visual_design: Typography and colour are restrained and consistent, numerals are tabular, and the list and tables look finished (list.jpg). The drawing undermines that. Line weights are good, but the oversized title-block text on short cartridges, the label sizes changing from page to page, and the mostly empty title-block frame make it look unbalanced. The overlapping R arrowheads look like an ink blot.
evidence.layout: The hierarchy is sound on every page: back link and Print, name, facts, drawing, then two table columns and the source footer. There are no overlaps or clipping. Space use is uneven: on 22 LR and 9 mm the title block takes more area than the drawing, and on long cases the drawing is a thin band. At 1280 px the Value column sits far from the Symbol column. Print fits on one page with whitespace left at the bottom.
evidence.usability: Searching, filtering, opening a cartridge, returning and printing each take one step. Search covers alternative names, there is an empty-state message, and every view has a bookmarkable hash URL. There is no sorting and no way to move to the next or previous cartridge. On short cartridges you have to scroll past a large title block to reach the tables.
evidence.reception: Reloaders and gunsmiths would trust the data presentation: exact values, DMS angles, tolerances in the tables and a clean print. Engineers would notice the 'Scale 1:1' claim, extension lines running through the part, and inconsistent label and title sizes. That reads as competent but not draughtsman-grade.

unmet_requirements: Title block states 'Scale 1:1', which is false on screen and in print (drawing.js:246)
Drawing labels leave out published tolerances (e.g. L1 39.62 without -0.2) (drawing.js:128-131)
Drawing legibility at phone width is not shown or tested; labels are a fixed 3 mm in a ~115 mm viewBox
Fillet radii that don't fit are silently reduced instead of being noted (geometry.js:74-78)
strengths: The geometry follows the brief's rules closely: rim types, chamfer, groove, belt, filleted shoulder, tangent ogive, heeled bullet, walls, solid head and primer pocket are each implemented and unit-tested, and outlines match the reference drawings
Data presentation is exact: published values, DMS angles, tolerances folded into the value, the specified symbols and units, grouped tables, search on alternative names and bookmarkable routes
Print is a clean single A4 page (header, full-width drawing, three-column tables, source footer), and an e2e test checks this for all 25 records
issues: Drawing readability is inconsistent: label and title-block sizes are fixed in mm, so short cartridges get huge text and a title block larger than the drawing, while long cases shrink to a thin strip (detail-22_long_rifle.jpg vs detail-9_3_x_74_r.jpg)

Drafting errors: diameter extension lines run from the feature through the case body, shoulder and section to the right-hand columns (drawing.js:214-215), the R arrowheads overlap on the short span, and 'Scale 1:1' is wrong
Maintainability gaps: no CI, no Node version pin, no changelog or ADRs, and the README points to a spec file that is not in the repository
review.verdict: This is a careful, well-tested build that implements nearly every rule in the brief, with accurate data tables and a working one-page print. Before publishing to a technical audience, the drawing needs size-independent label and title scaling, properly placed extension lines and a correct scale statement.
